title: Adoption mode becomes a checked key on every osf.toml read
summary: This change introduces a top-level `adoption_mode` key in a repository's own `osf.toml` and funnels every reader of that file through a single parse step, `config::repo_document`, which refuses an unsupported value. Previously each reader (`review_config`, `agents_config`, `changeset_risk::hot_paths`, `review_context::scan_config`) read and parsed the file on its own and silently fell back to defaults on a malformed file; now a bad value or an unreadable file stops the command with a message naming the key and the supported values. The layered `config::load` and the `--gate` load share the same parser, so `osf config show`, `lint writing --gate`, `agents list`, `review run` and `changeset risk` all refuse an unknown mode. `AdoptionMode` currently has one variant, `private-factory-repo`, and `require_adoption_mode` is added for commands that will depend on the mode, though none call it yet.

nodes.label: osf config show
nodes.subtitle: prints the layered config
nodes.summary: Reads the layered config through `config::load`, which now parses the repository's own osf.toml with `parse_repo_document` and refuses an unsupported adoption_mode.

nodes.label: osf lint writing --gate
nodes.subtitle: gate_must_explain_names
nodes.summary: The gate takes no setting from the repository's osf.toml but still parses it through `parse_repo_document`, so an unsupported adoption_mode stops the gate run.

nodes.label: osf agents list
nodes.subtitle: agents_config
nodes.summary: Reads the `[agents]` table through `agents_config`, which now delegates to `repo_document` and so inherits the adoption_mode check.

nodes.label: osf review run
nodes.subtitle: review pipeline
nodes.summary: Reads `[review]` through `review_config` and redacts lens context through `review_context::scan_config`; both now refuse an unsupported adoption_mode.

nodes.label: osf changeset risk
nodes.subtitle: assess
nodes.summary: `assess` calls `hot_paths`, which now returns a Result and propagates a config error instead of silently returning an empty glob list.

nodes.label: config::repo_document
nodes.subtitle: fn repo_document(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<toml::Value>, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: The one entry point for reading a repository's own osf.toml outside the layered load. Returns None when the file is absent, an error when it cannot be read or parsed, and otherwise the parsed document after `adoption_mode_of` has checked the key.

nodes.label: parse_repo_document
nodes.subtitle: fn parse_repo_document(text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<toml::Value, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: Parses osf.toml text and runs the adoption_mode check on the result. Shared by `repo_document` and the layered `load`, so neither path can skip the check.

nodes.label: AdoptionMode
nodes.subtitle: enum AdoptionMode { PrivateFactoryRepo }
nodes.summary: The top-level adoption_mode key of a repository's own osf.toml. One variant exists so far, `private-factory-repo`; `ALL` lists every supported mode and `name` gives the value written in the file.

nodes.label: adoption_mode_of
nodes.subtitle: fn adoption_mode_of(value: &toml::Value, path: &Path) -> Result<Option<AdoptionMode>, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: Checks the adoption_mode entry of an already parsed osf.toml. An absent key yields None; a value that is not a supported mode yields an error naming the key and the supported values.

nodes.label: config::require_adoption_mode
nodes.subtitle: fn require_adoption_mode(root, command, supported) -> Result<AdoptionMode, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: The mode a command needs: reads the key and checks it against the modes the command supports. An unset key is refused too, so a command never runs on a guessed mode. No command calls it yet.

nodes.label: config::load
nodes.subtitle: layered config merge
nodes.summary: Now parses the explicit config file with `parse_repo_document` and removes the adoption_mode key before merging, so the key never trips the struct's deny_unknown_fields.

nodes.label: review_config
nodes.subtitle: [review] table reader
nodes.summary: Delegates to `repo_document` instead of reading and parsing osf.toml itself, so an unsupported adoption_mode now stops it rather than being ignored.

nodes.label: agents_config
nodes.subtitle: [agents] table reader
nodes.summary: Delegates to `repo_document`; an absent file still yields the default AgentsConfig, but an unreadable or invalid file is now an error.

nodes.label: changeset_risk::hot_paths
nodes.subtitle: fn hot_paths(root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>
nodes.summary: Returns a Result now: an absent file yields an empty glob list, but an unreadable file, invalid TOML or unsupported adoption_mode propagates as an error to `assess`.

nodes.label: review_context::scan_config
nodes.subtitle: fn scan_config(config_root: &Path) -> Result<ScanConfig, String>
nodes.summary: Returns a Result now, so redaction stops on an unreadable or invalid osf.toml or an unsupported adoption_mode instead of falling back to compiled defaults.

nodes.label: redact_secrets
nodes.subtitle: lens context redaction
nodes.summary: Propagates the `scan_config` error with `?`, so a bad adoption_mode stops redaction before any lens context is built.

nodes.label: osf.toml
nodes.subtitle: repository's own config
nodes.summary: The file that now carries the top-level adoption_mode key. Absent means no mode; present but unreadable or invalid means an error.

nodes.label: layered config files
nodes.subtitle: --config, user, project layers
nodes.summary: The other layers merged by `config::load`. They share the parser with the repository's own file, so an unsupported adoption_mode in any of them is refused.

nodes.label: adoption_mode integration tests
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests/adoption_mode.rs
nodes.summary: Drives the CLI end to end: an unsupported mode stops `config show`, the gate path and `agents list`, naming the key and every supported value; a supported mode loads.

edges.label: loads config
edges.summary: `osf config show` renders the layered config, which parses the repository's own osf.toml through `parse_repo_document`.

edges.label: checks the mode
edges.summary: The gate takes no setting from the file but still parses it, so an unsupported adoption_mode stops the gate run.
`osf agents list` reads the `[agents]` table through `agents_config`.
`osf review run` redacts lens context through `redact_secrets`, which reads `[scan]` through `scan_config`.

edges.label: reads
edges.summary: `repo_document` reads `<root>/osf.toml`, returning None when it is absent and an error when it cannot be read.
`repo_document` hands the file text to `parse_repo_document`, which parses it and checks the mode.
Every parse runs the adoption_mode check, so no reader can skip it.
The check parses the raw value against `AdoptionMode::ALL` and names the supported values in the error.
`require_adoption_mode` reads the key and checks it against the modes the calling command supports.
The layered load shares the parser, so an unsupported mode in any layer is refused.
The layered load merges the explicit, user and project config files.
`review_config` now delegates to `repo_document` instead of parsing the file itself.
`hot_paths` now delegates to `repo_document` and propagates its error.
`scan_config` now delegates to `repo_document` and propagates its error.
The integration tests run the CLI against a repository whose osf.toml names an unsupported mode.

flows.title: Reading osf.toml and checking adoption_mode
flows.summary: Every reader of a repository's own osf.toml now goes through one parse step that checks the adoption_mode key. An absent file yields no mode; an unsupported value stops the command with a message naming the key and the supported values.

messages.label: Err: adoption_mode is vendored, not supported; supported values: private-factory-repo

views.title: Adoption mode check across osf.toml readers
views.summary: Every reader of a repository's own osf.toml now funnels through `config::repo_document`, which parses the file and checks the adoption_mode key. The layered load and the gate share the same parser.

views.title: Inside the config layer
views.summary: The parse-and-check step: `repo_document` reads the file, `parse_repo_document` parses it, `adoption_mode_of` checks the key against `AdoptionMode::ALL`, and `require_adoption_mode` is the entry point for commands that depend on the mode.
